Slapping

This Power Slap-inspired table game uses two competitors. The GM chooses a standard bout of three rounds or a title bout of five rounds. A coin toss decides who strikes first. The striker has 60 seconds to deliver an open-handed slap below the eye and above the chin. The receiver may not flinch, raise their shoulder, or tuck their chin, then has 60 seconds to recover and return to position.

Who rolls

PC competitors receive private requests to roll from an active actor owner. NPC competitors are rolled automatically by the GM. The striker rolls Athletics for slap effectiveness; the receiver rolls Fortitude for reaction and recovery. The module keeps both results private from the other competitor.

Judging and knockout

Each exchange uses a two-sided 10-point judging system. The better combined performance receives 10 points; the other receives 9, or 8 for a clear margin. An even exchange is scored 10–10. The judge considers the striker's effectiveness and the receiver's reaction and recovery. A critical slap against a critical receiver failure causes a knockout and ends the bout immediately. A critical striker result against a critical receiver failure is a knockout and ends the bout immediately.

If the bout reaches the scheduled rounds, the higher judge score wins. A tied standard or title bout receives one extra round. If that extra round is also tied, the official result is a draw.

Source acknowledgement. These Slapping rules are a table rule inspired by the user-provided Power Slap and Nevada State Athletic Commission description; they are not an official Power Slap rules implementation.
